subject: Pricing follow-up: token economics & benchmarking vs OpenAI/Anthropic/hosts
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Ellis <tim.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-12T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: token economics + benchmark ask

Hi Tim — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed on the call: 

Call recap (high level):
- Primary use case: customer support assistant + long-form summarization for enterprise docs.
- Expected usage profile: 5–10M tokens/month steady state, spikes to ~20M in seasonal months.  
- Latency SLO: P95 < 400ms for the LLM endpoint powering chat.
- Security: must support VPC/private deployment and KMS integration (covered in Private offering).

Commercial / cost ask from you: a target $/1M tokens target for budgeting and an idea of committed vs burst pricing. You mentioned a budget range you wanted to validate internally — below is what we pulled together so you have a single reference table.

Attached: redwood_token_pricing_calc.xlsx (pricing model + sample unit economics), benchmark_summary_q2_2026.pdf (public benchmarking vs major vendors).

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm the monthly steady-state volume (5–10M is our assumption). If higher, we can model different commit tiers.
2) Tell us the preferred model family (open-model like Llama/RedPajama vs closed models) and acceptable latency tradeoffs — those change unit economics.
3) We’ll produce a short price proposal (1–2 pages) with: committed tier pricing, burst rates, and a 60-day pilot/credit to validate latency and quality.

Benchmark snapshot (high level, per 1M tokens) — quick reference only:
- OpenAI (latest high-capacity chat model): ~$2,800–$3,500 / 1M tokens (hosted API list-level).
- Anthropic (high-capacity): ~$2,400–$3,000 / 1M tokens (hosted API list-level).
- Major open-model hosts (managed/open deployments): ~$900–$1,800 / 1M tokens (depends on quantization & commitment).
- Self-hosted/fully committed infra (customer/partner-managed): ~$400–$1,200 / 1M tokens (infra + ops costs vary).

What we can offer (Redwood):
- Hosted API (no commit): list-like pricing, typically aligned with public hosted ranges above.
- Dedicated / Reserved (monthly commit): we can get to $1,200–$1,800 / 1M tokens for open-model families with a 12-month commit at the volumes you described. Exact numbers depend on model family and quantization profile.
- Private on-prem/VPC: unit economics improve with larger commits; we’ll model this explicitly in the spreadsheet.

If you want, Marcus (cc’d) can run a line-by-line unit-economics model against your spike profile — Marcus, I flagged the sheet for the 5–10M / 20M spike scenario.

Thanks — looking forward to the preferred model family and confirmation on steady-state volume.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0192
From: Tim Ellis <tim.ellis@acme.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-04-12T18:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: token economics + benchmark ask

Thanks Vanessa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Volume: 5–10M/month is the right steady-state. We expect at least two months/quarter with spikes to ~20M for marketing pushes.
2) Model family: we prefer an open-model family (best-effort parity with Llama/RedPajama performance) if latency/quality tradeoffs are acceptable.
3) Target $/1M: procurement is aiming for a budgeting target of ~$1,500 / 1M tokens for evaluation. That’s our internal target for the pilot. If you can show committed pricing near that for the open-model family, we can move to procurement review.

Can you confirm whether the $1,200–$1,800 / 1M range you quoted for Dedicated applies to the *pilot* or only to full production commits? Also please flag any minimum monthly commit you would need to hit the low end of that range.

I’ll loop in procurement once we have a concrete 1–2 page price summary for the pilot and a draft SOW.

— Tim
Tim Ellis
Head of AI Products, Acme Corp
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Tim Ellis <tim.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-13T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: token economics + benchmark ask

Thanks Tim — good signal. Quick answers: 

- The $1,200–$1,800 / 1M *range* is achievable for Dedicated / Reserved with a 12-month commit at the volumes you cited. For a shorter pilot we generally price differently because we absorb more provisioning/ramp risk.

Pilot options we recommend: 
A) 60-day pilot (no long-term commit): blended rate typically in the $1,900–$2,400 / 1M tokens band for open-model families (we include a pilot credit to offset setup + validation). Pilot is ideal to validate latency, correctness, and integration.
B) Pilot with a small commitment (3-month trial commit with a modest monthly minimum): we can get to $1,500 / 1M for the pilot if you commit to a 3-month minimum of 6M tokens/month. This is a structured approach we’ve used with other enterprise customers.

Minimums to hit the $1,200 low-end: typically a 12-month commit at ~10M tokens/month or higher (exact thresholds depend on the model family and quantization profile). We’ll model those exact thresholds in the attached workbook.

Marcus — can you run the 3 scenarios in the spreadsheet (60-day no-commit pilot, 3-month small commit @6M/mo, 12-month commit @10M/mo) and return a one-pager with the effective $/1M and headline terms? We’ll attach that for procurement.

Next steps: 
- Marcus to produce one-pager + updated workbook (today)
- Vanessa to produce a 1–2 page pilot price summary and draft SOW (tomorrow)
- Tim to confirm which pilot option procurement prefers so we can route to contract

— Vanessa

> On Apr 12, 2026, at 18:03, Tim Ellis <tim.ellis@acme.com> wrote:
>
> Thanks Vanessa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:
> 1) Volume: 5–10M/month is the right steady-state.
> 2) Model family: prefer open-model family (Llama/RedPajama parity).
> 3) Target $/1M: procurement aiming for ~$1,500 / 1M tokens.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Tim Ellis <tim.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-13T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: token economics + benchmark ask

Hi all — ran the three scenarios in the attached workbook and pulled headline numbers into the one-pager (attached as benchmark_summary_q2_2026.pdf and updated redwood_token_pricing_calc.xlsx):

Headlines (effective $/1M tokens, open-model family):
- 60-day no-commit pilot (pilot credits applied): $2,100 / 1M effective
- 3-month small commit (6M/mo floor): $1,480 / 1M effective
- 12-month commit (10M/mo floor): $1,180 / 1M effective

Notes:
- The 3-month small commit hits Tim’s target of ~$1,500 / 1M and is feasible to operationalize quickly. We assume quantized model runtimes (8-bit) and moderate KV-cache hit rates for the pricing.
- To get to the 12-month $1,180 number we need the 10M/mo floor and agreement to the standard data handling/retention terms (we flagged those in the workbook).
- The hosted API list prices for comparison are included in the PDF appendix (OpenAI/Anthropic list-levels) — our model shows Redwood Dedicated with a 12-month commit is roughly ~30–60% cheaper than those hosted list prices for open-model families at the volumes you quoted.

Attached: benchmark_summary_q2_2026.pdf (one-pager) and updated redwood_token_pricing_calc.xlsx (scenario tab updated).

Next: Vanessa will push the 1–2 page pilot summary and draft SOW; Tim, if procurement is comfortable, the 3-month small commit is the fastest path to hit your ~$1,500 target.

— Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
